question: How can one two-view loss update student parameters by gradient, teacher parameters by averaging, and a separate center state from raw teacher outputs without conflating their roles or timing?
element_groups: Two augmented view identities reused by both networks; same architecture, distinct student/teacher parameters.
Per-view n-by-K raw outputs, K-axis probabilities, teacher-only current center and stopped targets.
Two opposite-view H terms, each row-mean cross-entropy, combined by average.
Current/new student and old/new teacher parameter states; gradient and teacher EMA have different ownership.
Current/new K-vector center and mean of stored raw teacher logits across 2n rows; separate running state.

Teacher subtracts current C before temperature softmax; stopped teacher targets supervise opposite-view student predictions without category labels.

Full multicrop view set and pair-sum scope differ from two-view average; downstream representation is backbone f output.

visual_design: Panel A current computation/loss; B parameter updates; C center-state update. Repeated explicit aliases avoid crossed long connections without adding networks/views. Solid data arrows, dashed gradient/parameter arrows and dotted state arrows plus color/text distinguish roles; next-iteration dependencies use explicit text.
transferable_rules: Stop gradient does not establish permanently frozen teacher weights; name gradient, parameter averaging and running-state updates separately.
State each update input owner, mathematical object, aggregation axis and old/new iteration; confirm order from the current source.
Same architecture does not mean tied parameter state. Separate momentum parameters do not necessarily have unequal numerical values.
Preserve scope and normalization when simplifying multi-view losses; a pair sum and a two-term average cannot be silently equated.
